title: seri.ai Mobile Touch Walkthrough Evidence
summary: Mobile walkthrough notes for dense review surfaces where first-time visitors need to tap, scan, scroll, and recover context without treating seri.ai as a static screenshot.
principle: Mobile quality is not proven by a responsive screenshot alone; the route must preserve task intent, reachable controls, labelled actions, and context recovery while keeping unsupported claims visible.
limitations: This is source-validated walkthrough evidence, not external reviewer feedback.
This is not a physical-device lab run.
A future real-device pass should verify touch comfort, scroll fatigue, graph readability, and hesitation points with first-time reviewers.

routes.visitorTask: Ask a public-safe question, submit it, inspect the answer packet, follow a related source, and recover the public-safe boundary.
routes.startingSignal: The route opens with Ask Ravikanth as an evidence console over Ravikanth's public professional graph rather than a generic chatbot.
touchTargets: Ask input labelled Ask a question about Ravikanth Seri's public work
Send message button labelled Send message
walkthroughSteps: Tap the input and enter a safe question about Operational Intelligence or Ravikanth's public evidence.
Tap Send message and confirm the assistant returns a reviewable answer packet.
Scan source coverage, boundary, related routes, latency, and AI-disclosure state.
Tap a related route or source link and confirm the path remains public-safe.
Return to Ask and confirm the question context remains understandable.
sourceEvidence: components/chat.tsx exposes labelled input and send controls.
Ask response metadata displays source coverage, boundary, related route, latency, and AI disclosure.
Ask fixtures validate refusal, routing, citations, and identity-mark behavior.
observedPasses: Primary input and send action have accessible labels.
Mobile prompt grid is responsive and validated by viewport contracts.
Fallback behavior avoids inventing answers when the API fails.
remainingRisks: No reviewer-labeled live answer quality baseline exists.
Long answers may still create scroll fatigue on small devices.

routes.visitorTask: Start with the live investigation graph, step through evidence/replay/hypotheses/action gate/release gate, toggle evidence, and inspect the decision packet.
routes.startingSignal: The route opens with the signature artifact and prioritizes the graph over long explanatory copy on mobile.
walkthroughSteps: Open the route at mobile width and confirm the live investigation graph is visible before deep explanatory content.
Tap each step in the five-part investigation sequence and confirm the active state changes.
Toggle at least one evidence item and confirm the graph and confidence context preserve contradiction and missing evidence.
Select a hypothesis and inspect support, contradiction, and missing-evidence conditions.
Inspect the action gate and confirm human approval remains explicit before operational change.
sourceEvidence: app/investigation-room/page.tsx suppresses secondary desktop links on mobile.
app/simulator/simulator.tsx contains labelled graph summaries, evidence taxonomy, missing evidence, contradiction, and human approval sections.
Viewport validation requires mobile first viewport to prioritize the live investigation graph.
observedPasses: Mobile first viewport includes the investigation graph and H1.
Interactive controls are buttons, not inert visual decoration.
Observation, inference, contradiction, missing evidence, confirmed fact, and approval gate are represented in the workbench.
remainingRisks: The route remains the heaviest experience and needs real-device interaction-latency evidence.
External reviewers still need to judge whether the graph feels product-grade rather than demo-like.

routes.visitorTask: Use mobile contents, scan the doctrine, ask follow-up questions, and continue into related reading without losing orientation.
routes.startingSignal: The doctrine page exposes Contents and Ask questions before the long body on mobile.
walkthroughSteps: Open the doctrine page and confirm the mobile contents block appears before the article body.
Tap at least one contents anchor and confirm the reader can jump into the document.
Tap an Ask-question shortcut and confirm the prompt routes into Ask.
Return to the doctrine and inspect related reading.
Confirm tables and dense sections remain horizontally contained.
sourceEvidence: app/wiki/[slug]/page.tsx includes mobile contents, Ask questions, table fallbacks, related reading, and version history.
Accessibility validation checks wiki headings, table mobile cells, and related navigation contracts.
Visual QA captured the doctrine at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths without horizontal overflow.
observedPasses: The page has a mobile reading scaffold instead of a raw long essay.
Ask shortcuts create a task-oriented path out of dense doctrine.
remainingRisks: No external reader has confirmed whether the doctrine is still too dense on mobile.
Footnote-heavy sections may require further reading-comfort tuning.

routes.visitorTask: Inspect the thesis spine, market signals, source evidence, and falsification posture from a mobile viewport.
routes.startingSignal: The route frames LinkedIn themes as testable claims instead of social proof.
walkthroughSteps: Open Radar and confirm the thesis spine appears before market signals.
Scroll into public thought process and inspect the claim-to-evidence structure.
Tap the Evidence Pack link and confirm the proof posture is reachable.
Inspect trend source links and confirm external links are labelled.
Return to Radar and confirm no horizontal overflow from dense trend rows.
sourceEvidence: app/radar/page.tsx uses min-w-0 layouts and labelled external source links.
Viewport contracts validate Radar responsive structure.
Search retrieval routes observability-thesis and market-signal queries to Radar.
observedPasses: Radar presents public writing as testable thesis evidence.
Dense rows use responsive grid constraints.
External source links include evidence-type labels.
remainingRisks: Real visitors may need clearer priority between market trend, Ravikanth angle, and falsification question.
External link behavior has not been tested with live browser history on physical mobile devices.

routes.visitorTask: Understand Ravikanth's operating arc, inspect public code/LinkedIn links, review project proof, and find background or resume evidence.
routes.startingSignal: The route presents an operating record, not a generic portfolio grid.
walkthroughSteps: Open Work and confirm the first screen states the operating record behind Operational Intelligence.
Tap GitHub and LinkedIn links only as public profile exits, not as proof of private production claims.
Scroll through operating arc and project proof cards.
Tap an architecture judgment ledger item and confirm it routes to an inspectable public surface.
Use the review spine to continue toward doctrine, reference architecture, Operations Room, or resume.
sourceEvidence: app/work/page.tsx exposes public-code boundaries, LinkedIn/GitHub links, operating arc, project proof, and review spine.
Public Project Proof Ledger states what each project proves and does not prove.
Visual QA captured Work at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths without horizontal overflow.
observedPasses: The page keeps Ravikanth, public work, and evidence connected.

remainingRisks: External reviewers still need to confirm whether the career-to-work path is immediately obvious.
Public repositories need deeper runnable examples before project proof can reach the highest bar.
